title: Probability Distributions
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is a Random Variable (r.v.)?
cards.a: A real-valued function X whose domain is the sample space S of a random experiment and range is a subset of real numbers R (X: S → R).
cards.hint: Assigns a single numerical value to each outcome of the random experiment.

cards.q: Discrete Random Variable vs Continuous Random Variable?
cards.a:
Discrete r.v.: Takes countable values (finite or countably infinite, e.g. number of heads: 0, 1, 2).
Continuous r.v.: Takes any real value in an interval [a, b] (uncountable, e.g. height, time, temperature).
cards.hint: Discrete is characterized by p.m.f.; Continuous is characterized by p.d.f.

cards.q: Two mandatory conditions for a valid Probability Mass Function (p.m.f.) P(X = xᵢ) = pᵢ?
cards.a:
1. pᵢ ≥ 0 for all possible values xᵢ.
2. ∑ pᵢ = 1 (total probability must equal 1).
cards.hint: Used in 2-mark questions to find an unknown constant k.

cards.q: Cumulative Distribution Function (c.d.f.) F(x) for a discrete random variable?
cards.a: F(x) = P(X ≤ x) = ∑_{xᵢ ≤ x} P(X = xᵢ).
cards.hint: F(x) is a non-decreasing step function. 0 ≤ F(x) ≤ 1, F(-∞) = 0, F(∞) = 1.

cards.q: Discrete r.v. formula: Find P(X = xᵢ) from c.d.f. F(x)?
cards.a: P(X = xᵢ) = F(xᵢ) - F(x_{i-1}).
cards.hint: Subtract the previous cumulative probability from the current one.

cards.q: Expected Value (Mean) E(X) or μ of a discrete random variable?
cards.a: E(X) = μ = ∑ xᵢ · P(X = xᵢ) = ∑ xᵢ · pᵢ.
cards.hint: Represents the long-term average or center of gravity of the distribution.

cards.q: Variance Var(X) and Standard Deviation σ of a discrete random variable?
cards.a:
Var(X) = σ² = E(X²) - [ E(X) ]² = ∑ xᵢ² pᵢ - [ ∑ xᵢ pᵢ ]².
Standard Deviation: σ = √Var(X).
cards.hint: Var(X) can NEVER be negative! If you get a negative value, recheck your arithmetic.

cards.q: Linear transformation properties of Expectation and Variance?
cards.a:
E(aX + b) = a · E(X) + b
Var(aX + b) = a² · Var(X)
SD(aX + b) = |a| · SD(X).
cards.hint: Adding constant b shifts mean by b, but has ZERO effect on variance! Scalar 'a' gets squared in variance.

cards.q: Two mandatory conditions for a valid Probability Density Function (p.d.f.) f(x)?
cards.a:
1. f(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ R.
2. ∫_(-∞)^∞ f(x) dx = 1 (total area under the density curve is 1).
cards.hint: Set integral = 1 to solve for unknown constant k.

cards.q: Probability of interval for a continuous random variable with p.d.f. f(x)?
cards.a: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫_a^b f(x) dx.
cards.hint: Geometrically: The area under the curve f(x) between x = a and x = b.

cards.q: CRITICAL TRAP: For a continuous random variable, what is P(X = c) at an exact point?
cards.a:
P(X = c) = 0 for ANY single exact point c!
Consequently: P(a < X < b) = P(a ≤ X < b) = P(a < X ≤ b) = P(a ≤ X ≤ b).
cards.hint: Area under a single point (line of width 0) is 0. Strict vs non-strict inequalities make NO difference in continuous distributions!

cards.q: Cumulative Distribution Function (c.d.f.) F(x) of a continuous random variable?
cards.hint: f(x) is the derivative of F(x): f(x) = F'(x) = d/dx [ F(x) ].

cards.q: Expected Value E(X) and Variance Var(X) for a continuous random variable?
cards.a:
E(X) = μ = ∫_(-∞)^∞ x · f(x) dx
Var(X) = E(X²) - [ E(X) ]² = ∫_(-∞)^∞ x² · f(x) dx - μ².
cards.hint: Analogous to discrete formulas: replace ∑ with ∫.

cards.q: How to find the Median M of a continuous random variable?
cards.a: Solve for M such that P(X ≤ M) = 1/2 ⇒ F(M) = 1/2 ⇒ ∫_(-∞)^M f(x) dx = 0.5.
cards.hint: The median divides total probability area exactly in half (50% on each side).

cards.q: Uniform (Rectangular) Distribution on interval [a, b]: p.d.f., Mean, and Variance?
cards.a:
p.d.f.: f(x) = 1 / (b - a)  for a ≤ x ≤ b (and 0 elsewhere).
Mean: E(X) = (a + b) / 2
Variance: Var(X) = (b - a)² / 12.
cards.hint: Standard MHT-CET shortcut: Variance is always (length of interval)² / 12.

cards.q: Can a p.d.f. f(x) have values greater than 1?
cards.a: YES! f(x) is a probability DENSITY, not a probability. Only its integral must equal 1.
cards.hint: Example: If X is uniform on [0, 0.5], then f(x) = 1 / 0.5 = 2 for x ∈ [0, 0.5].

cards.q: If X and Y are independent random variables, what are E(XY) and Var(X ± Y)?
cards.a:
E(X Y) = E(X) · E(Y)
Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y)
Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
cards.hint: Variance is ALWAYS additive: Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y), never minus!

cards.q: Expectation and Variance of a constant c?
cards.a:
E(c) = c
Var(c) = 0.
cards.hint: A constant has zero spread/dispersion, so its variance is 0.

cards.q: If p.m.f. of X is P(X = x) = k x for x = 1, 2, 3, 4, find k.
cards.hint: Sum all probabilities and equate to 1.

cards.q: If p.d.f. of X is f(x) = k x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 (and 0 otherwise), find k and E(X).
cards.hint: First find k using total integral = 1, then compute E(X) = ∫ x f(x) dx.

cards.q: Discrete probability interval relation using c.d.f. F(x)?
cards.a: P(a < X ≤ b) = F(b) - F(a).
cards.hint: Notice lower bound is strict (<) and upper bound is inclusive (≤).

cards.q: A coin is tossed 3 times. Let X be number of heads. Find E(X) and Var(X).
cards.hint: Also matches Binomial B(3, 1/2): Mean = np = 1.5, Var = npq = 3/4.

cards.q: Two dice are rolled. Let X be sum of numbers. What is E(X)?
cards.hint: Symmetry shortcut: Range is 2 to 12, symmetric around the center value 7.

cards.q: Can Var(X) ever be equal to 0?
cards.a: YES, if and only if X is a constant (degenerate random variable taking a single value with probability 1).
cards.hint: If Var(X) = 0, there is zero variability; X is deterministic.

cards.q: Given F(x) = x²/9 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, find p.d.f. f(x) and P(1 ≤ X ≤ 2).
cards.hint: Using c.d.f. F(2) - F(1) is faster than integrating f(x) from 1 to 2!
